solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sea fish caught on Welsh river

indicators.note: in a down-free across clue 'on' simply places one piece next to the other, here the first before the second

blocks.note: c. is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the Usk flows through south Wales to the Severn estuary

explanation.surface: An angler lands a sea fish while fishing a river in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The cusk is a cod-like food fish of the North Atlantic, also called the torsk.

clue.text: Child slicing a corm’s misused old spade

indicators.note: something slicing into another cuts its way inside it, so one piece goes into the middle of the other
letters that are misused are put to the wrong order, so the phrase before it is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
ch. is the dictionary abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: A child cuts into a corm with an antique spade it is misusing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Child sits within the rearranged letters, not at either end. A caschrom is a Gaelic implement from the Scottish Highlands and islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A caschrom is a Highland foot-plough, a crooked spade once used for tilling crofts.

clue.text: Dame’s place once for Scots chemise

blocks.note: first meaning: the Channel Island long ruled by the Dame of ...
second meaning: a Scottish word for a shirt or shift

explanation.walkthrough: Sark is a small Channel Island whose hereditary ruler, Dame Sibyl Hathaway, governed it for much of the twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: The island was the Dame's fief, and in Scots dialect the same word names a shirt or undergarment.

clue.text: Name in floor peg? It reveals fault in timber

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is held inside it

blocks.note: to floor someone is to knock them out, a KO
N is the abbreviation for name
a thole is the peg in a boat's gunwale that holds an oar

explanation.surface: Someone spots a name on a peg in the floorboards, and wonders about a flaw in the wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floor' is a verb, to knock down, not the boards underfoot; a thole is a rowlock peg.
explanation.definitionFit: A knothole is the gap left where a knot has dropped out of a plank, a visible defect in wood.

clue.text: Russian spy unit treads westward, extremely racist? Not I

indicators.note: in an across clue going westward means reading right to left
says the letter i must be left out of the word before

blocks.note: treads are the steps of a staircase
a Nazi is an extreme racist

explanation.surface: A Russian unit marches west, though its members deny being extreme racists.
explanation.definitionFit: Spetsnaz are Russian special forces, originally a military intelligence and sabotage arm of the GRU.

clue.text: Night owl resolute about work (7, two words)

indicators.note: one word placed about another wraps around it

blocks.note: stout means firm and determined
op. is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A determined night owl keeps going round the clock at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop-out is someone who habitually stays out late at night, a late-hours reveller.

clue.text: Helping of fettucine, dealt up, blissful

indicators.note: a helping is just a portion of the dish, so the letters lie inside the words that follow
in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A serving of pasta handed out leaves a diner in bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: Edenic means like the Garden of Eden, paradisal and so supremely happy.

clue.text: Central American found in Atlantic Ocean

indicators.note: the letters are located inside the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A traveller from Central America turns up in mid-ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Tico is the informal name for a Costa Rican, a native of a Central American country.

clue.text: Modern trendy, joker in Rhine heading north (7, two words)

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means the river's name is read bottom to top
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a rhine, also spelt reen, is a drainage ditch in Somerset
a wag is a joker

explanation.surface: A trendy joker is spotted on the Rhine, sailing upstream.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital R hides a common noun: a rhine is a West Country ditch, not the German river.
explanation.definitionFit: A New Ager follows the alternative modern movement of crystals and holistic beliefs, a fashionable type.

clue.text: Dancing a conga gaily? Not quite striving for high ideals

indicators.note: not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped from the word before it
the letters move about as a dancer does

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: Joining a conga with abandon is hardly the act of someone with lofty ideals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' trims the final letter of gaily before the eleven letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Anagogical describes the mystical, spiritual reading of scripture, reaching upward toward heavenly meaning.

clue.text: Erstwhile footie star to take dinner out weekly?

indicators.note: taken out means removed from the name before it

blocks.note: Zinedine Zidane, retired French football great
to dine is to take dinner

explanation.surface: A retired football star is invited to dinner out once a week.
explanation.walkthrough: Footie is British slang for football (soccer). The question mark flags weekly as just one example of a periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: A zine is a small self-published magazine, and a weekly is one kind of periodical publication.

clue.text: A male child at home with little energy requiring treatment for flu

blocks.note: taken as written
a man is a male
a tad is a small child
someone at home is in
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A man with a child at home is low on energy and needs flu medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Amantadine is an antiviral drug used against influenza A, and also for Parkinson's disease.

clue.text: Set out to capture castle, a blow of old

indicators.note: set out means laid out afresh, so these letters are rearranged
what captures something holds it inside

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
the rook is the chess castle

explanation.surface: An army sets out to seize a castle, striking a blow in the old style.
explanation.definitionFit: Strooke is an archaic spelling of stroke, meaning a hit or strike.

clue.text: Loud troupe in the wars, what cavalrymen may dread

indicators.note: something in the wars is battered and knocked about, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A noisy troupe of soldiers in battle is a horror for any cavalryman.
explanation.definitionFit: A trou-de-loup is a conical pit with a stake in it, a trap dug to stop charging horses.

clue.text: Trumpeter maybe showing off abandoned by king

indicators.note: the word left behind by the next one loses it

blocks.note: swank is showy display
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A trumpeter's showing off loses the king's favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trumpeter' looks like a musician, but it is a breed of bird; 'maybe' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The trumpeter is the largest North American species of swan, named for its loud call.

clue.text: Red wine, ordinary, taken in measure, mature

indicators.note: something taken in is held within another

blocks.note: a pint is a measure
O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: An ordinary red, served by the measure, is best when given time to mature.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinotage is a South African red grape, a cross of Pinot Noir and Cinsaut, and its wine.

clue.text: Coarse fellow, Henry or Bill, in poetry

blocks.note: a hog is a coarse, greedy person
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A boorish man named Henry, or Bill, turns up in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill is not a name here but a headland, as in Portland Bill; 'in poetry' marks Spenser's word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogh is Spenser's form of hoe, a promontory or headland, which is what a bill is.

clue.text: Swirling fogs hid such as Dagon

indicators.note: swirling things are churned about, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Swirling mists concealed an ancient idol.
explanation.definitionFit: Dagon was a Philistine deity long depicted as half fish, an example of a fish-god.

clue.text: A lady mostly dressed in sacking? A dazzler often

indicators.note: mostly means all but the end, so the last letter goes
to dress is also to arrange, as soldiers dress their ranks, so the letters are put into a new order
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: hemp is coarse fabric used for sacks
taken as written
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: A lady wearing sackcloth is hardly dazzling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed' reads as clothing beside 'sacking', but it does a second job here, arranging the shortened letters before they go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Car headlamps on full beam often blind oncoming drivers, so a headlamp is a common dazzler.

clue.text: Those getting kitted up? They may be Welsh

blocks.note: first meaning: people who dress
second meaning: kitchen sideboards with shelves, a classic Welsh style

explanation.walkthrough: A Welsh dresser is a sideboard with open shelves above for crockery, a familiar British furniture style.
explanation.definitionFit: People who put clothes on are dressers, and a dresser is also a piece of kitchen furniture.

clue.text: Spell of contact sport? It’s murder

blocks.note: RU is rugby union, a contact sport
a bout is a spell of activity

explanation.surface: A session of rough contact sport is described as absolute murder.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces sit in the reverse order of the clue: the sport comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubout is American slang for a killing, from rub out meaning eliminate.

clue.text: Canoe? One difficult to understand sailor holds up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up reads the word from bottom to top
what holds something has it inside

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
dark can mean obscure
AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A puzzled sailor stuck holding up a canoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A bidarka is an Alaskan sea kayak made of skins on a frame, a type of canoe.

clue.text: Relic of old rock chap found in wild Eire

indicators.note: located inside, so the man is placed within the other letters
wild letters are out of order and need rearranging

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man discovered in the Irish wilds is a fossil of an old rocker.
explanation.definitionFit: Remanié is geological debris, a fragment of an older rock or fossil reworked into a newer deposit.

clue.text: Idle chat from peevish old fellow cop ignored after noon

indicators.note: the word that is ignored is left out of the one before
places the shortened word behind the letter for the time of day

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for noon
attercop is an old dialect word for a spider and for a crabbed person
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumpy old man rambles on, and the police officer ignores him after lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: To natter is to chatter idly, and as a noun it means a gossipy chat.

clue.text: Catch that is supplied with locks for Edmund?

blocks.note: to catch a word is to hear it
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A doorman catches what is said about fitting locks for someone called Edmund.
explanation.walkthrough: Locks are hair, not door fittings, and Edmund is Edmund Spenser, whose spelling this is.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearie is Spenser's spelling of hairy, and having plenty of locks means being hairy.

clue.text: Casualty transport serving some maimed evacuees

indicators.note: the answer serves only some of the letters, a part of the words that follow

blocks.note: runs from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: An ambulance flight carries wounded people evacuated from a war zone.
explanation.definitionFit: Medevac is medical evacuation, usually by helicopter, moving injured people to hospital.

clue.text: Medical personnel perform with gas

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the two parts are joined end to end

blocks.note: to do is to perform
CS gas is the tear gas used in riot control

explanation.surface: Hospital staff carry out treatment using anaesthetic gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Docs is the informal plural for doctors, the physicians of a medical team.

clue.text: Sri Lanka, southern, mostly producing skinny layers

indicators.note: mostly means all but the end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: CL is the international vehicle code for Sri Lanka, from Ceylon
austral means southern

explanation.surface: Sri Lanka's southern region yields thin strata.
explanation.definitionFit: Claustra, plural of claustrum, are thin sheets of grey matter in the brain.

clue.text: Rosette, dear in e.g. Savoy

blocks.note: first meaning: a knot of ribbon or soft rosette ornament
second meaning: French term of endearment, also French for cabbage, as the Savoy is

explanation.walkthrough: Savoy is a French region, and a savoy is a kind of cabbage; either way the French word for darling fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Chou is a dressmaker's ribbon rosette and the French pet name meaning darling, literally cabbage.

clue.text: Local closed, group getting hot inside

indicators.note: the group getting a thing means receiving it
inside places the letter within the other word

blocks.note: a set is a group
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: The pub has shut because the crowd inside was overheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like a pub, a British sense; here it marks a dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shet is a regional dialect form of shut, so in local speech it means closed.

clue.text: Garment made of yarn, primarily Arabian

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter counts

blocks.note: abb is the woof yarn in weaving
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A robe woven from yarn, Arab in origin.
explanation.walkthrough: Yarn suggests a story, but here it is weaving thread.
explanation.definitionFit: An abba, or aba, is a loose sleeveless outer robe worn by Arabs, made of camel or goat hair.

clue.text: Dance music performed by singers out of bounds?

indicators.note: the bounds are the word's edges, and these are removed

blocks.note: choral music is sung by a choir

explanation.surface: Singers stray off limits while a dance tune is performed.
explanation.definitionFit: The hora is a lively circle dance from Romania and Israel.

clue.text: Panel holds nurse fit for defence

indicators.note: what holds something has it inside

blocks.note: a table can be a flat panel or slab
EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A tribunal panel includes a nurse fit to give evidence for the defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable position is one that can be held or defended against attack.

clue.text: Part of ship’s frames, bent keel rim crafted with no length

indicators.note: length is abbreviated to one letter, which is to be left out
something crafted is made up afresh, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shipwright crafts a keel and rim from bent timbers, cutting them short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'crafted' does the rearranging once L for length leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A knee-timber is a bent piece of wood forming an angled brace, a knee, in a ship's frame.

clue.text: Javanese mulberry? Erect one alongside highway mostly

indicators.note: alongside means next to, so the parts are placed end to end
mostly means all but the last letter

blocks.note: erect means upright, up
a is one
a street is a public road

explanation.surface: Someone plants a Javanese tree by the side of the main road.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas is a poisonous tree of Java belonging to the mulberry family, Moraceae.

clue.text: Foreign country is profitable

blocks.note: first meaning: the French word for country
second meaning: brings in money

explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign' signals a word from another language, here French.
explanation.definitionFit: Pays is French for land or region, and English pays means yields a profit.
